recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Fishermen** in Kozhikode are reporting significantly reduced catches and higher fish prices due to rising sea surface temperatures (SST) and the El Niño effect. **Scientists at the ICAR-Central Marine Fisheries Research Institute (CMFRI)** attribute the decline to plankton migrating into deeper waters, forcing fish to follow their food source.  **Boat owners** in the region are struggling with low catches, high fuel costs, and declining incomes, leading to reduced harbour activity and a decrease in migrant workers from other states.

recent_articles.title: Sagar Mitras thank Nellore MP for six-month extension of PMMSY scheme - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Nellore MP Vemireddy Prabhakar Reddy** met with members of the A.P. Sagar Mitra Employees Union to discuss the extension of the Pradhan Mantri Madhya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) welfare scheme. **Mr. Reddy** had previously requested an extension from the Union Minister for Fisheries, **Rajiv Ranjan Singh**, and explained that the six-month extension would allow the Sagar Mitras to continue serving as a bridge between the government and fishermen in coastal villages.

recent_articles.title: Children with Special Needs from State-run schools in Andhra Pradesh scale Everest Base Camp, set national benchmark - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Twenty-one children with special needs** from government schools in Andhra Pradesh successfully completed the Everest Base Camp trek in Nepal. The 16-day expedition, organized by **Samagra Shiksha**, Andhra Pradesh, and supported by the School Education Department, marked the first government-sponsored Everest Base Camp trek for specially-abled students.  The students, accompanied by mountaineers and officials, demonstrated their determination to overcome social stigma and achieve their goals. **Nara Lokesh**, HRD Minister and IT Minister of Andhra Pradesh, congratulated the students on their success and highlighted the importance of inclusivity in education.

recent_articles.title: Telangana IT Minister Sridhar Babu calls for stricter curbs against gutka, pan masala, khaini and drugs in State - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Duddilla Sridhar Babu**, **Telangana IT Minister**, warned against the consumption of gutka, pan masala, khaini, and narcotics, emphasizing their serious health risks. He urged young people to avoid addiction and adopt healthier lifestyles during an Oral Cancer Awareness Marathon in Hyderabad organized by the **Global Oral Cancer Trust**.  **Cyberabad Police Commissioner M. Ramesh** also participated in the event, flagging off a 5K run.

recent_articles.title: Census 2027: States asked to identify vulnerable areas, keep biased enumerators out - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India (RG&CCI)** has instructed State Directorates to identify vulnerable populations during the ongoing Census exercise, including those affected by communal or political tensions. The RG&CCI emphasized avoiding enumerators with biases towards specific social or religious communities and ensuring all individuals are counted without omission, as any inaccuracies could lead to legal challenges.  The census is being conducted in two phases: Housing Listing and Housing Census (HLO) from April 1 to September 30, followed by Population Enumeration in February 2027. The RG&CCI has also outlined specific guidelines for enumerators, including the preference for teachers and local officials familiar with the area.

recent_articles.title: Tagged Olive Ridley turtles from T.N. reach Sri Lanka Dome, reveal migration patterns - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Environment, Climate Change and Forests Secretary Supriya Sahu** announced that **Olive Ridley turtles** from Tamil Nadu have begun migrating towards the Sri Lanka Dome.  Sahu stated that turtles released from Tamil Nadu's coast have already reached the Sri Lanka Dome, a region known for its high marine life concentration. Turtles migrating from Odisha are also expected to join them in this shared marine hotspot shaped by oceanic processes.

recent_articles.title: Shuttered filling stations, restricted sales fuel anxiety in Andhra Pradesh - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Andhra Pradesh** is experiencing a sudden fuel shortage of both petrol and diesel, leaving many retail outlets dry. **The State government**, **oil marketing companies**, and **IndianOil** have assured the public that there is sufficient stock to last for the next 15 days. However, commuters, farmers, aqua farmers, and transport operators are facing difficulties due to long queues at limited functional filling stations.  Despite assurances from oil companies, the disconnect between port logistics and retail outlets continues to leave citizens waiting in line.

recent_articles.title: Birds of Mangalajodi: A visual journey into Chilika’s avian paradise - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Dr. Srinivasa Rao Somanchi** and his late wife, **Dr. Seetha Khambhampati**, authored the photographic book "Birds of Mangalajodi," a tribute to the wetlands' birdlife. The book features striking photographs capturing the diverse species found in this significant waterfowl habitat.  The couple spent years documenting the wetlands together, with **Mr. Srinivasa Reddy**, Fellow of The Royal Photographic Society of Great Britain, praising their dedication and the book's message of passion overcoming age. Wildlife photography enthusiasts will find "Birds of Mangalajodi" invaluable for its insights into capturing birds in their natural habitat.

recent_articles.title: Mahanadi tribunal gives last opportunity to Odisha, Chhattisgarh to settle river water dispute - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Mahanadi Water Disputes Tribunal (MWDT)**, chaired by former Supreme Court Judge Justice Bela M. Trivedi, is nearing a decision on the water sharing formula between **Odisha** and **Chhattisgarh**. The tribunal has given both states one last opportunity to finalize their proposals for mutual settlement by May 2, 2026, or face its own formulation.  The MWDT expressed dissatisfaction with the lack of concrete proposals and urged both parties to address the issues promptly.

recent_articles.title: Samrat Choudhary approves funds for 75 ITI in first Cabinet meeting as Bihar CM - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary** approved several initiatives during his first Cabinet meeting, including the establishment of 75 state-of-the-art Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) under the **PM SETU** scheme. The Cabinet also sanctioned ₹305 crore for an 11-acre research park at IIT Patna and an additional grant of ₹39 crore for phase 2 of the Incubation Centre at IIT Patna.  The State Cabinet also decided to develop 11 new satellite townships in the state, prohibiting land sales and construction until a Master Plan is prepared.

recent_articles.title: BJD expresses concern over deletion of 9.8 lakh voters’ names from list ahead of SIR in the State - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Biju Janata Dal (BJD)** protested the deletion of 9.8 lakh voters from electoral rolls in Odisha ahead of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) process. The party expressed concern over potential disenfranchisement and urged for safeguards to prevent further deletions, particularly for migrant workers who may be wrongly removed due to their absence during verification.  The BJD emphasized that NRI voters should not be disenfranchised and called for humane and inclusive verification procedures to ensure voter rights are protected.
